description: Heritage `value of … for key` and its Core `:d["k"]` twin report the SEMANTIC stage identically (issue #755). Both lines name the same undefined operand, and both raise `ol-undefined-var` with `params` `{ name: "nope" }` — the learner's own variable and nothing else. The `value` head word does NOT appear in any structured param, on either side: diagnostic identity is `code` plus `params` and the same condition must keep the same params (`spec/error-model.md:254-259`), while Heritage is alternate spellings only (`spec/conformance.md:150`). The two diagnostics differ only in `source_span`, which points where each learner wrote the operand. This is the stack-neutral twin of the parse/semantic-stage guard in `packages/parser/src/heritage-canonical-diagnostic-params.test.mjs`; with Heritage ACTIVE the reader raises nothing of its own at this stage, so its own failures (`ol-unknown-key`, `ol-type`) are runtime-stage and fixtured under `../execution/`. Heritage depends on Data (`spec/conformance.md:305`), so both `data` and `heritage` are active.

diagnostics.message: :nope is not defined yet. declare it with a parameter, 'local', or an assignment first.
